Issued at 344 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast: Split flow pattern continues across 
eastern North America...with an impressive southern branch closed 
low lifting northeast through the Mid Atlantic region (-2 to -3 
sigma 500mb height anomaly)...strong zonal northern branch flow 
displaced well to the north from Hudson Bay to Newfoundland.  Narrow 
but extensive axis of deep layer moisture (trowal) wrapping around 
this cyclone across the upper Lakes into the mid Mississippi Valley. 
Pattern across the west is more consolidated and dominated by flow 
coming around an upper low northeast of Hawaii.  Short wave trough 
that crashed ashore over the Pacific Northwest/British Columbia on 
Thanksgiving Day now moving through central Canada and the northern 
High Plains.  994mb occluded low over western New York/Lake Erie... 
having reformed farther inland from an initial coastal cyclone whose 
dynamic umbilical cord outran it.  Strong north/northeast boundary 
layer flow across Michigan to the west of this low.  

Pacific energy will carve out a new trough across the central CONUS 
for the coming weekend...actually a bit of a split trough with 
stronger negative height anomalies in the southern portion of the 
trough over the Ohio/Tennessee Valleys.  Northern portion of this 
trough will swing through the Great Lakes later Sunday into 
Monday...then pattern turns more zonal across eastern North America 
as a split trough reaches the west coast (with a lot of energy in 
the southern branch heading into southern California and the Baja 
Peninsula). This pattern continues through midweek...southern branch 
upper low moving into the Desert Southwest with consolidated zonal 
flow across the eastern CONUS.  Great Lakes looks to be in the 
confluence axis between the northern and southern branches 
(baroclinicity anyone?)...could see some impacts from southern 
branch short wave trough toward the end of next week.

Negatively tilted short wave trough will cross Michigan Saturday... 
followed by above mentioned northern branch wave for later Sunday. 
But main surface reflection will be with the southern branch 
wave...grabbing a lee cyclone over the southern High Plains and 
spinning it up as it tracks from the Ozarks to the lower Lakes 
Sunday/Sunday night.  Quick shot of colder air crosses the region 
Monday in the cyclonic wake of this system...but a ridge of high 
pressure returns Tuesday with southerly return flow for midweek.  

Primary Forecast Concerns:  

Lingering rain band across southeast counties tonight: Trowal/ 
deformation rain band associated with the occluded cyclone over the 
lower Lakes stretches from southwest Quebec...across Lake Huron and 
clipping portions of the forecast area adjacent to Saginaw Bay. 
Northwestern edge of the rain band has been butting up against some 
very dry air...with pockets of single digit dew points across 
eastern Upper and interior northern Lower.  During the late 
afternoon rain band should pivot to more of a north-south 
orientation...remaining east of the I-75 corridor and then pushing 
out into Lake Huron toward midnight at the latest.  

Some showers possible Saturday with short wave trough passage: Next 
wave in the series coming across northwest Ontario/upper Midwest 
this afternoon...narrow/broken band of precipitation associated with 
it.  This short wave trough is expected to become negatively tilted 
and swing northeast across Michigan Saturday...and bringing its band 
of light showers along with it.  Would expect most of this activity 
to be east of the forecast area shortly after sunset. 

More widespread precipitation chances Sunday (at least across Lower 
Michigan): A much better chance for precipitation is in the offing 
for Sunday...within the deformation zone of a low expected to track 
from southern Missouri to the lower Great Lakes by Monday morning. 
Precipitation shield spreads into the area Sunday morning... 
deformation axis will serve as a "limiting streamline" as far as 
westward extent of precipitation is concerned.  So a west-east PoP 
gradient is in order across the area...highest probabilities (like 
today) south of an MBL-PZQ line.  Back edge of precipitation shield 
moves into Lake Huron Sunday night...though could see rain change to 
snow along the back edge.  Low level cold air comes in on its 
heels...and should see some lake convection develop perhaps as early 
as late Sunday afternoon (more on that below). 

Colder air arrives Sunday night/Monday...lake induced convection 
likely:  Deep layer northwest flow develops across the upper Lakes 
Sunday night in the wake of the surface low moving through the lower 
Lakes.  850mb temperatures eventually dropping to -8C or so will 
allow for lake bands to develop...with precipitation type trending 
toward snow as the boundary layer gets colder.  Lake effect should 
continue into Monday.

Some low probabilities for precipitation Tuesday as warm air begins
